title: Why Lettuce Keeps Being Linked to Foodborne Illness Outbreaks: What Consumers Should Know

body_text: Lettuce is one of the most popular vegetables in the world. It appears in salads, sandwiches, wraps, burgers, and countless ready-to-eat meals. Many people consider leafy greens an essential part of a healthy diet because they provide vitamins, minerals, fiber, and hydration. However, lettuce has also become a recurring concern in food safety discussions. Over the years, several outbreaks of foodborne illness have been connected to contaminated leafy greens, including illnesses caused by parasites, bacteria, and other harmful microorganisms. Recent cases involving contaminated lettuce have once again raised an important question: why does this simple vegetable seem to be linked to illness so often? The answer involves a combination of farming conditions, how lettuce is handled, the way people eat it, and the challenges involved in removing dangerous contaminants. Lettuce Is Widely Consumed, Increasing the Chance of Problems One reason lettuce appears frequently in food safety reports is simply because people eat a lot of it. Leafy greens are a common ingredient in everyday meals, meaning that if a contaminated batch enters the food supply, many people may be exposed. In the United States, lettuce consumption is especially high. Millions of people eat salads and other lettuce-based foods regularly, creating a large pathway for potential outbreaks. A food product that is eaten frequently and distributed widely has a greater chance of causing a large outbreak if contamination occurs. Lettuce Grows Close to the Ground The growing environment of lettuce is another important factor. Unlike some fruits and vegetables that grow on trees or above the soil, lettuce grows close to the ground. This makes it more vulnerable to contact with contaminated soil, irrigation water, animal waste, or other sources of microorganisms. One of the biggest concerns in agriculture is contaminated water. If irrigation systems use water containing harmful bacteria or parasites, those organisms can spread across crops before they reach consumers. Experts have suggested that contaminated water is a possible contributor to some major leafy green outbreaks because large amounts of produce may be exposed during farming. The Structure of Lettuce Makes Cleaning Difficult Lettuce leaves have a unique structure that can make them challenging to clean thoroughly. The leaves contain folds, layers, and uneven surfaces where bacteria and parasites can hide. Unlike smooth-skinned produce such as apples or cucumbers, lettuce does not have a simple surface that can easily be scrubbed. Small cracks, damaged areas, or broken leaves can create additional opportunities for microorganisms to enter and remain protected. Even careful washing at home may not completely remove every harmful organism that is attached to the leaves. Raw Foods Do Not Get a Safety Step From Cooking Cooking is one of the most effective ways to destroy many harmful microbes. Heat can kill certain bacteria and parasites that may cause illness. The challenge with lettuce is that it is usually eaten raw. Salads, sandwiches, and wraps typically use fresh lettuce without a cooking step that would reduce contamination risks. If harmful organisms are present, they can remain on the food until it is eaten. This is also why other raw ingredients, including fresh herbs such as cilantro and parsley, have occasionally been investigated during foodborne illness outbreaks. Pre-Washed Lettuce Is Not Always Risk-Free Many consumers choose packaged lettuce because it is convenient. Products labeled as washed, triple-washed, or ready-to-eat may seem safer because they require less preparation. However, washing processes cannot guarantee that every microorganism has been removed. Some contaminants may stick tightly to leaves or survive processing. While commercial washing systems are designed to improve safety, no method can completely eliminate all risks. Consumers should still handle packaged greens carefully and follow storage instructions. Common Illnesses Associated With Contaminated Lettuce Lettuce has been connected with several types of foodborne illnesses over the years. One concern is cyclosporiasis , an intestinal illness caused by the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis . Symptoms can include prolonged diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and dehydration. Some people may require medical attention if symptoms become severe. Leafy greens have also been associated with bacterial illnesses caused by pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella . These infections can lead to stomach pain, diarrhea, fever, and other health complications. The severity of illness depends on factors such as the type of pathogen involved, the amount consumed, and a person’s overall health. How Consumers Can Reduce Their Risk Although food safety concerns are real, people do not need to avoid lettuce completely. Leafy greens can still be part of a balanced diet when handled properly. Here are some steps that may help reduce risk: Wash Fresh Produce Properly Rinse lettuce leaves under clean running water before eating. Remove damaged outer leaves and separate leaves so water can reach more surfaces. Avoid using soap or household cleaning products on food because they are not designed for consumption. Keep Produce Refrigerated Proper storage slows the growth of many harmful microorganisms. Store lettuce in the refrigerator and avoid leaving it at room temperature for long periods. Prevent Cross-Contamination Use clean hands, utensils, and cutting surfaces when preparing lettuce. Keep raw meat, poultry, and seafood separate from fresh produce. Pay Attention to Food Recalls Government agencies and food companies sometimes issue recalls when contamination is suspected. Staying informed can help consumers avoid products that may pose a risk. A Balanced Approach to Food Safety Foodborne illness outbreaks linked to lettuce can be alarming, especially because many people associate salads with healthy eating. However, these incidents do not mean that all lettuce is unsafe. The larger issue is understanding how contamination happens and how the food system works to reduce risks. Farmers, food manufacturers, retailers, regulators, and consumers all play a role in keeping produce safe. Improvements in farming practices, water monitoring, processing methods, and consumer awareness can help reduce future outbreaks. Fresh vegetables remain an important part of a healthy diet. The goal is not to eliminate them, but to make informed choices and practice safe food handling. Sources U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA): Food safety information on fresh produce and leafy greens Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC): Information on foodborne illnesses and outbreak investigations United States Department of Agriculture (USDA): Food handling and produce safety guidance University extension food safety resources on fresh produce contamination risks Disclaimer This article is for informational purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice. If you experience severe symptoms such as persistent diarrhea, dehydration, high fever, blood in stool, or symptoms lasting several days, seek guidance from a qualified healthcare professional.

title: Keeping Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations and PostgreSQL in Step
summary: Two-way sync between Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations and PostgreSQL, done right: field-level change detection, origin tracking, and conflict resolution, not…
body_text: Plenty of products need what lives in Dynamics 365 F&O, order status, credit limits, invoice balances, without making users log into the ERP. The usual answer is to pull that data into the app's own PostgreSQL database. The moment you do, you have two copies of the same records, and they start to drift. Keeping them in step is a two-way sync problem. This guide is about doing that properly: what two-way sync means when one side is an ERP and the other is a Postgres app database, how a record moves through its sync lifecycle, and why field-level sync beats a pair of one-way exports. The setup assumes a two-way sync platform such as Stacksync between F&O and Postgres. The Dynamics 365 connector and PostgreSQL connector pages cover the surface; here we focus on keeping the two consistent. Why an app keeps a local copy of F&O data Your product cannot make thousands of users hit the F&O OData endpoints directly. It is too slow for an app UI, and it would trip priority-based throttling in minutes. So the app keeps the data it needs, customers, orders, balances, in its own Postgres database, where reads are fast and under your control. That local copy is only useful if it is accurate. If a payment posts in F&O and the app still shows an open balance, or a customer updates an address in the app and F&O never hears about it, the copy is worse than no copy, because people trust it. Two-way sync is what keeps the copy honest. What two-way sync actually means here Two one-way exports are not a two-way sync. A pair of scripts, one F&O-to-Postgres and one Postgres-to-F&O, will fight each other: each treats the other's write as a fresh change and echoes it back, and when both sides edit the same record, one blindly overwrites the other. A real two-way sync puts an engine in the middle. The engine in the middle is what makes it a sync, not two exports pointed at each other. The engine does three things a pair of scripts cannot: it detects changes at the field level so only what moved is synced, it tracks the origin of every change so a write does not loop back, and it resolves conflicts under one shared policy when both sides touch the same field. That is the difference between two databases that agree and two databases that argue. The life of a synced record It helps to follow one change through the system. An edit in either F&O or Postgres enters a lifecycle: detected, mapped, applied, and confirmed, with branches for conflicts and for throttling. One record's path: detected to confirmed, with conflict and throttling handled, not dropped. When a write is throttled, F&O returns a 429 and the engine backs off and retries rather than dropping the change. When both sides changed the same record, the engine merges at the field level and re-applies the winner. Only when the target acknowledges the write is the record marked confirmed and both sides declared in sync. Nothing is silently lost, and nothing loops. One-way export vs two-way sync The pair-of-scripts approach looks cheaper on day one. The table lays out what it actually costs every day after. Two one-way exports Field-level two-way sync Consistency Drifts between runs Both sides match in seconds Echo loops Each write re-triggers the other Origin tracking stops the loop Conflicts Last write wins, blindly Merged per field, one policy Load on F&O Full pulls trip throttling Only changed fields Operations Two scripts to babysit One engine, monitored, retried Two exports look cheaper on day one and cost more every day after, in drift and reconciliation. That daily cost shows up as reconciliation, as support tickets about wrong balances, and as the engineer who owns the cron jobs. A real two-way sync moves that cost off your plate, and it is the same engine that keeps F&O and Snowflake in step, so a second pairing is configuration, not a second project. Two databases, one truth Keeping Dynamics 365 F&O and PostgreSQL in step is not about copying data faster. It is about an engine that detects field-level changes, tracks their origin, and resolves conflicts, so the app's local copy is always something users can trust. Set that up once and the drift, the echo loops, and the reconciliation go away. Stacksync is built for exactly this: real-time, field-level, origin-aware two-way sync between F&O and Postgres, with backoff that respects F&O throttling. To keep your own app database and F&O consistent, book a demo .

title: Is Your Student Engagement Platform Actually Accessible? 5 Questions to Ask
summary: Most campuses assume their student engagement platform accessibility is covered. These five questions reveal where the real gaps tend to hide before they grow.
body_text: Most institutions approach student engagement platform accessibility as a simple question: “Are we compliant or not?” They evaluate their platform, check it against a standard, and move on. But accessibility works differently in practice, and the gap between compliance in theory and accessibility in real life is where students, staff, and administrators struggle every day. Extended compliance timelines can create a false sense of security, but accessibility gaps tend to grow over time, not shrink. A platform can align with certain standards on paper and still create friction for students, staff, and administrators trying to use it every day. As platforms evolve, new features, content, and workflows can introduce issues over time, even in systems that have already been evaluated. As accessibility expectations continue to evolve, a better question is: Can people actually use your platform without barriers? Here are five questions that can help you find out. 1. Can users complete critical tasks without assistance? Accessibility is not just about whether a feature exists. It is about whether someone can use it independently from start to finish. Think about the tasks that matter most on your campus when assessing your platform’s accessibility. For example: Can a student register for an event using only a keyboard? Can an administrator manage a form using a screen reader from start to finish? These are the kinds of tasks your platform needs to support every single day. In many cases, accessibility gaps do not appear in static evaluations. They show up when users try to complete real tasks and hit a wall somewhere in the process. A practical indicator of accessibility is simple: Can users complete core tasks without friction or workarounds? 2. Is accessibility integrated into the platform or added on later? Some platforms rely on overlays or separate accessibility modes. Others are designed to support accessibility as part of the core experience. This distinction matters. Overlays and separate accessibility modes are common, but are also a sign that accessibility was not a part of the original build. These add-ons can introduce inconsistencies that only become apparent when obstacles arise during real use. When accessibility is integrated into the platform itself, it can adapt more naturally to different input methods, including keyboard navigation, screen readers, and zoomed interfaces. In many cases, well-designed platforms aim to support accessibility by default, rather than requiring users to enable it separately. 3. How does your platform handle real-world content? Accessibility does not stop at the platform itself. Every event, image, and form introduces new variables and potential gaps. This means the responsibility of ensuring accessibility is always shared between the platform and the institution using it. For example, platforms can provide the ability to add alternative text, but they cannot write that text themselves. They can flag low color contrast in a template, but they cannot prevent staff from overriding corrections. This is where the people using the platforms come into play. Accessibility outcomes depend on both the platforms that enable them and how higher ed teams use them. Accessibility is a shared responsibility between technology and the institution. 4. Are you aligned with standards and continuously improving? Most institutions look to standards like WCAG and Section 508 as benchmarks. But alignment is not a one-time milestone. Standards and expectations continue to evolve. In practice, accessibility requires: Ongoing evaluation across a large and evolving set of user interaction paths. Testing across browsers, devices, and commonly used assistive technologies such as NVDA, VoiceOver, and TalkBack. Frequent updates and improvements as the platform evolves. This often includes reviewing a wide range of user workflows and refining them over time as new features are introduced. Accessibility efforts typically prioritize high-impact workflows such as navigation, events, and forms, where users interact most frequently. Rather than focusing on a single point-in-time status, strong platforms demonstrate consistent progress toward alignment over time. 5. Do you have visibility into progress and gaps? Accessibility should not operate as a black box. Institutions benefit from understanding: What areas have been evaluated. What improvements are being made. Where gaps may still exist. This often includes documentation, roadmaps, or ongoing updates that reflect how accessibility is being maintained over time. Without visibility, it becomes difficult to measure progress or make informed decisions about your platform. Ongoing Accessibility Management Accessibility is not something you finish. It is something you manage. Accessibility expectations evolve as platforms update, content changes, user needs shift, and standards develop. What institutions can do is build practices that treat accessibility as an ongoing operational priority rather than a one-time check. This requires continued attention to both the platform itself and its use within the institution. As the landscape of accessibility continues to shift, the institutions that stay ahead will be the ones asking better questions and choosing platforms that support change over time. If accessibility is on your radar, now is the time to take a closer look before small gaps become larger risks. If you’re evaluating accessibility across your platform, we can walk through what to look for and how institutions are approaching it today. Learn more about CampusGroups .

title: Wyoming LLC paying contractors in Mexico: what to check
summary: A practical checklist for Wyoming LLCs and other US entities paying contractors in Mexico: onboarding, MXN payouts, records, and recurring payroll workflow.
body_text: A Wyoming LLC can be a simple US entity structure for a founder. Paying contractors in Mexico from that company is a different question. The payment workflow has to handle US funding, MXN delivery, contractor expectations, and clean records for bookkeeping. This is especially important when the team is paid on a recurring schedule. Checklist before paying contractors in Mexico Before running the first payroll batch, confirm: the legal name of the US company; who controls and approves payments; contractor names and bank-account details; whether each contractor should receive MXN or USD; how the FX conversion is approved; what payment proof the contractor receives; how the payment will appear in bookkeeping; who handles follow-up if a payment is delayed. The more recurring the contractor list is, the more valuable it is to turn this into a template. Why entity eligibility matters Some financial tools support only certain entity types, states, or onboarding profiles. A founder may have a valid US company and still discover that a specific tool does not support the exact setup. That is why a contractor-payment workflow should start with onboarding reality, not just a landing-page promise. For Coba, eligibility is reviewed through the onboarding and compliance process. US LLCs can be a fit when the company has a real business need for cross-border payments and can provide the required company and owner information. Keep the records simple When a US company pays Mexico contractors, finance usually needs to know: the original USD funding amount; the MXN amount received; the FX rate or spread context; the contractor or invoice reference; the proof of payment; the date funds were released and received. If those details are scattered across messages and bank screens, payroll becomes harder to audit later. Where Coba fits Coba Banking helps US companies create cleaner USD/MXN operating flows for Mexico payments. For contractor payroll, that can mean recurring payment templates, MXN payouts, status visibility, and a clearer path from payment to proof. Explore Coba Banking or request pricing .

title: How Wix Store Owners in India Can Accept International Card Payments Without a Second Gateway
summary: Many Indian Wix stores lose NRI and international customers because overseas cards aren't enabled by default. Learn how to accept international payments on Wix using Cashfree Payments without managing a second payment gateway.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle TL;DR: If your Wix store serves NRI or international customers, accepting only domestic payment methods can lead to abandoned checkouts. With Cashfree Payments, eligible merchants can enable international Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Maestro cards, along with PayPal and Apple Pay support, from the same Wix integration—without signing up for a separate payment gateway. Why International Buyers Can’t Pay on Many Wix Stores Launching a Wix store in India is relatively straightforward. Most businesses can quickly start accepting UPI, domestic debit and credit cards, net banking, and other popular local payment methods. The challenge often appears only after international customers begin placing orders. Imagine an NRI customer in the UK discovers your Ayurvedic skincare brand through Google or social media. They browse your products, add items to their cart, and proceed to checkout using a UK-issued Visa card. Instead of completing the payment, the transaction fails or the customer abandons the purchase because their preferred payment method isn’t supported. For many merchants, this looks like an abandoned cart rather than a payment failure, making it difficult to identify the actual issue. This isn’t a bug in Wix. It’s simply the result of many Indian stores being configured primarily for domestic payments. If your business serves customers outside India, even occasionally, your checkout should support the payment methods those buyers expect. Default Wix Checkout vs. Wix + Cashfree Payments Feature Default Wix Setup Wix + Cashfree Payments* UPI ✅ ✅ Domestic Debit & Credit Cards ✅ ✅ Net Banking ✅ ✅ International Visa & Mastercard ❌ ✅ International Amex & Maestro ❌ ✅ Apple Pay (International) ❌ ✅ PayPal Requires separate setup Supported after connecting PayPal Multi-currency Display Limited Supports 140+ currencies Single Dashboard for Domestic & International Payments ❌ ✅ *International payment methods are available for eligible merchants after activation within the Cashfree Payments dashboard. Why NRI Buyers Matter For many Indian D2C brands, NRI customers represent one of the highest-intent customer segments. Unlike first-time international shoppers, NRIs are already familiar with Indian products, brands, and cultural preferences. They’re often looking specifically for products they cannot easily purchase in their local market. Examples include: Ayurveda and wellness products Regional food and snacks Traditional clothing and handloom Handmade jewellery Religious and festive products Baby and family care products made in India These customers frequently arrive with a clear purchase intent. Losing them because their international card isn’t accepted is entirely avoidable. What You Need to Accept International Payments on Wix Supporting international buyers requires more than enabling another payment option. A complete cross-border payment setup typically includes the following layers. Payment Layer Purpose Domestic Payment Gateway Accepts UPI, domestic cards, wallets, net banking, and other India-specific payment methods. International Card Acceptance Enables Visa, Mastercard, Amex, and Maestro cards issued outside India. Cross-border Payment Infrastructure Allows compliant international payment collection through an RBI-authorized payment aggregator. Multi-currency Display Lets overseas buyers view prices in their preferred currency, improving checkout confidence. Cashfree’s Wix payment gateway combines these capabilities within a single merchant account. Eligible merchants can enable international card acceptance directly from their Cashfree dashboard rather than opening and managing a separate payment gateway account. International card acceptance is activated inside the Cashfree account under Settings → Payment Methods . PayPal support is available by connecting your PayPal account separately. How International Checkout Works with Cashfree Payments Once international payments are enabled, overseas buyers enjoy a checkout experience that’s similar to any global ecommerce store. For example, a customer in Canada can complete payment using a Canadian-issued Mastercard without being redirected to another website or asked to use an alternative payment method. From the merchant’s perspective, both domestic and international transactions appear in the same Cashfree Payments dashboard, simplifying reconciliation and reporting. International settlements are typically processed in INR on a standard T+2 settlement cycle. Businesses with larger export volumes can discuss EEFC account settlement options with the Cashfree team, subject to eligibility. The result is a unified payment workflow without maintaining separate payment gateways for domestic and international customers. Ready to Accept International Payments on Wix? Enable international cards, Apple Pay, and PayPal through a single Wix integration with Cashfree Payments-no second payment gateway required. Explore Wix Payment Gateway Common Reasons International Cards Still Fail Even after integrating a payment gateway, international transactions may not work if certain settings haven’t been completed. Some common causes include: International card acceptance hasn’t been activated in the Cashfree dashboard. PayPal hasn’t been connected (if you intend to offer PayPal). Another payment provider is still configured as the active Wix payment method. The merchant account hasn’t yet been approved for international payment acceptance. Sandbox or test mode is still enabled. Reviewing these settings before going live can help reduce checkout failures and improve conversion rates. How to Enable International Payments on Your Wix Store Setting up international payments doesn’t require a second payment gateway. If you’re already using Cashfree Payments with Wix , most of the work involves enabling the right payment methods within your merchant account. Step 1: Verify Your Cashfree Payments Account Log in to your Cashfree Payments dashboard and confirm your account is fully activated. If you plan to accept overseas payments, ensure your account is eligible for international payment acceptance. Step 2: Enable International Cards Navigate to Settings → Payment Gateway → Payment Methods and verify that international card acceptance is enabled for supported credit and debit cards. If you don’t see this option, contact the Cashfree Payments support team to request activation. Step 3: Connect Cashfree Payments to Wix In your Wix dashboard, confirm that Cashfree Payments is configured as your active payment gateway. International card acceptance works through the Cashfree integration, so another gateway may not support the same capabilities. Step 4: Connect PayPal (Optional) If your customers prefer PayPal, connect your PayPal account from the Cashfree Payments dashboard. Once linked, PayPal becomes available as an additional payment option for eligible international buyers. Step 5: Review Settlement Preferences International payments are generally settled in INR on a T+2 settlement cycle. If your business handles significant export volumes, you can discuss EEFC account settlement options with the Cashfree Payments team, subject to eligibility. Step 6: Test Before Going Live Before launching, complete a few test transactions to verify that: International cards are accepted successfully. Payment confirmations are received. Orders are created correctly in Wix. Settlement and reporting appear correctly in your Cashfree dashboard. A quick end-to-end test can help prevent unnecessary checkout failures after launch. Businesses That Benefit Most from International Payments Not every online store has overseas customers, but for some categories, international demand is already built into the business. International payment support is particularly valuable for: Ayurveda and wellness brands selling authentic India-made products. Regional foods and specialty snacks popular with the Indian diaspora. Handmade jewellery and artisan products purchased for gifting and cultural occasions. Handloom, ethnic wear, and traditional textiles serving overseas Indian communities. Baby and family care products formulated specifically for Indian consumers. If your website already receives traffic from countries such as the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, Singapore, or the UAE, enabling international payments can help convert visitors who are already ready to buy . The Bottom Line If your Wix store attracts NRI or international customers, your checkout should support the payment methods they expect. Otherwise, you risk losing high-intent buyers at the final step of the purchase journey. With Cashfree Payments, eligible merchants can enable international card acceptance from the same Wix integration without managing a separate payment gateway. A few minutes spent on setup can help deliver a smoother checkout experience for customers around the world. Does Cashfree Payments support cross-border payment collection? Yes. title: Fortune 50 Employer Awards Dario Contract to Deliver AI-Powered Cardiometabolic Care Platform
summary: Contract award for over 100,000 eligible employees marks Dario's fifth Fortune 50 client, further reflecting growing demand among large employers for integrated, outcomes-driven chronic condition...
body_text: Press Releases Fortune 50 Employer Awards Dario Contract to Deliver AI-Powered Cardiometabolic Care Platform Contract award for over 100,000 eligible employees marks Dario's fifth Fortune 50 client, further reflecting growing demand among large employers for integrated, outcomes-driven chronic condition management Program expected to launch Fall 2026, with revenue contribution beginning by year-end and ramping through 2027 NEW YORK , July 16, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- DarioHealth Corp. (NASDAQ: DRIO) (the "Company", "DarioHealth" or "Dario"), a leading AI-powered healthcare technology company transforming the management of chronic conditions, today announced another Fortune 50 employer has selected Dario to provide its integrated digital cardiometabolic care platform for employees living with diabetes and/or hypertension. The program will be available to more than 100,000 eligible employees and is expected to launch in Fall 2026. Eligible members will receive a unified care experience that combines connected devices, personalized human coaching, AI-driven insights via DarioIQ™ and behavior change support within a single platform. Annual recurring revenue from the program is expected to begin by the end of 2026 following implementation, with increasing contribution anticipated throughout 2027 and beyond. "Winning another Fortune 50 employer underscores the growing recognition that integrated chronic condition management delivers better outcomes than treating each condition independently, resulting in clinically significant outcomes and economic impact," said Erez Raphael, Chief Executive Officer of Dario. "The value we deliver to the largest enterprises in the world is evident in the fact that nearly one-quarter of our clients today are Fortune 500 companies." "Employers continue to focus on managing healthcare costs while simultaneously improving health outcomes. Our AI-enabled multi-condition platform, powered by DarioIQ, is uniquely positioned to deliver on both objectives," added Lara Dodo, Dario's Chief Operating Officer. Unlike traditional point solutions that manage individual conditions, Dario's integrated chronic condition platform is designed to address comorbidities, including diabetes and hypertension , two of the most prevalent and costly chronic diseases that frequently occur together – costing a combined $500+ billion in U.S. healthcare costs annually. Published research shows that members on Dario's digital platform managing three chronic conditions (diabetes, hypertension and overweight) simultaneously experience better outcomes than those who manage just one condition. About DarioHealth Corp. (Nasdaq: DRIO) DarioHealth (Nasdaq:DRIO) is an AI-powered healthcare technology company helping health plans, health systems and employers improve health outcomes while lowering the cost of care. The Company's integrated platform combines connected devices, personalized member engagement, AI-driven insights and provider-backed clinical care to support people living with conditions including diabetes, hypertension, weight management, musculoskeletal and behavioral health needs. Powered by more than 13 billion proprietary longitudinal healthcare data points collected over more than a decade, Dario's AI platform personalizes care at the individual member level by analyzing biometric, clinical and behavioral data to deliver more timely and effective interventions. By combining engagement, clinical intelligence and care delivery within a single platform, Dario helps customers address multiple chronic conditions through one solution. title: Illumina appoints Michael Sullivan Chief Commercial Officer and Julie Coletti Chief Legal Officer
summary: New leaders bring extensive leadership experience across life sciences, diagnostics, and medical technology SAN DIEGO, July 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Illumina, Inc. (NASDAQ: ILMN) today announced the appointment of Mike Sullivan as Chief Commercial Officer, effective July 20, 2026, and Julie Coletti
body_text: Illumina appoints Michael Sullivan Chief Commercial Officer and Julie Coletti Chief Legal Officer July 9, 2026 PDF Version New leaders bring extensive leadership experience across life sciences, diagnostics, and medical technology SAN DIEGO , July 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Illumina, Inc. (NASDAQ: ILMN) today announced the appointment of Mike Sullivan as Chief Commercial Officer, effective July 20, 2026, and Julie Coletti as Chief Legal Officer, effective August 3, 2026. The appointments add experienced leaders to Illumina's Executive Leadership Team as the company continues advancing its strategy, serving customers, driving growth, and delivering on its mission to improve human health around the world. "We are excited to welcome Mike and Julie to Illumina," said Jacob Thaysen, chief executive officer of Illumina. "Mike brings deep commercial expertise, a customer-first mindset, and significant experience scaling global organizations, while Julie is a highly accomplished legal and business leader with deep experience across the life sciences and medical technology sectors. I look forward to working closely with both of them as we continue helping customers unlock new insights across genomics, multiomics, and human health." Sullivan will be responsible for leading Illumina's global commercial organization. He brings more than 30 years of commercial leadership experience across diagnostics, precision medicine, healthcare, and life sciences, with a proven track record of driving growth, expanding customer adoption, and leading high-performing global teams. Most recently, Sullivan served as Chief Commercial Officer at Caris Life Sciences, where he led the company's global commercial operations across oncology diagnostics and precision medicine. Prior to Caris, he held senior commercial leadership roles at Roche Diagnostics, Ortho Clinical Diagnostics, IDEXX Laboratories, and Abbott Diagnostics. As Chief Legal Officer, Coletti will lead Illumina's global legal, regulatory, and government affairs teams and serve as corporate secretary to the Illumina Board of Directors. Coletti joins with extensive legal, regulatory, and governance expertise across the life sciences and medical technology sectors. Previously, Coletti served as Chief Legal and Regulatory Officer at Align Technology. Prior to that, she held senior legal leadership positions at Danaher Corporation and Bayer HealthCare, advising executive leaders and boards of directors on a broad range of complex issues, including compliance matters, intellectual property, competition, governance, and public policy. She also serves as a director for Fortis Life Sciences, a provider of solutions to life science and diagnostic companies. About Illumina Illumina is improving human health by unlocking the power of the genome. Our focus on innovation has established us as a global leader in DNA sequencing and array-based technologies, serving customers in the research, clinical, and applied markets. Our products are used for applications in the life sciences, oncology, reproductive health, agriculture, and other emerging segments. To learn more, visit illumina.com and connect with us on X , Facebook , LinkedIn , Instagram , TikTok , and YouTube .
